drills.title: Build a first program
drills.prompt: Arrange the lines into a runnable program. Two lines do not belong. (The editor indents by braces for you.)
drills.explain: Java wants every program inside a class, and the computer starts at main. Statements end with ;, blocks sit between { and }, and main must be public static void main(String[] args).

drills.title: Printing tricks
drills.prompt: Fill the blanks so the program prints the goal output.
drills.explain: print writes without a new line, so the next println continues on the same line. printf fills %d (whole number) and %n (new line). "=".repeat(20) repeats a text 20 times.

drills.title: Text or number?
drills.prompt: Read the code and type exactly what it prints, one line per line of output.
drills.explain: Numbers are added (5) but text in quotes is shown as written. \n starts a new line. print leaves the cursor on the same line, so ...done continues after Loading.

drills.title: Java is case-sensitive
drills.prompt: This program does not compile. Click the line the compiler complains about, then choose the fix.
drills.explain: System is a class, so it starts with a capital S. The compiler reads system as an unknown package and says so, pointing at the line number. Fix the first compiler error first.

drills.title: Review the AI's receipt printer
drills.prompt: An AI assistant wrote this receipt printer. It compiles, but tick the real problems (there are two).

issues.text: The total line prints Total: 3050 instead of 80
issues.why: "Total: " + 30 is text, and + 50 then glues 50 on as text. Add first: "Total: " + (30 + 50).

issues.text: The prices are typed again in the total, so they can drift apart
issues.why: Keep each price in one variable and reuse it, so the lines and the total always agree.

non_issues.text: class Receipt must be declared public to run
non_issues.why: java Receipt.java runs a non-public class too. public is only required when the file name must match.

non_issues.text: println does not move to a new line
non_issues.why: println does end the line; print is the one that does not.
main is void: it returns nothing.

drills.explain: With text, + joins left to right: "Total: " + 30 + 50 builds the text first. When reviewing generated code, look at every + that mixes text and numbers.
